title: Distinct Subsequences II
summary: Calculate the count of unique non-empty subsequences in a given string, modulo 10^9 + 7.
statement: Calculate the count of unique non-empty subsequences in a given string, modulo 10^9 + 7. A subsequence is formed by removing characters from the original string without changing the order of the remaining characters.
hints: Appending c doubles subsequences before removing duplicates created at its previous occurrence.
Track total including empty and the old total saved for each ending character.
The subtracted family is exactly the subsequences that previously acquired the same final c.
editorial: The subtracted family is exactly the subsequences that previously acquired the same final c.

tests.explanation: The seven nonempty subsets of positions produce seven different subsequences.
The distinct results are a,b,aa,ab,ba,aba: six.
